title: Costa Rica Nomad Visa: Requirements and How to Apply | Grey
summary: Costa Rica's digital nomad visa lets remote workers live legally for up to two years. Requirements, costs and application process explained. Apply now.
body_markdown:
I first heard about Costa Rica in 2012 when my brother was exploring options for his master’s degree abroad. At the time, it was just another country name to me, but it kept coming up in conversations about quality of life, education, and stability in Central America. Years later, I began to see a different side of it, one shaped not just by academics or tourism, but by lifestyle.


That shift became more real with the introduction of Costa Rica’s digital nomad visa in 2021, which allows remote workers to live in the country for up to two years, renewable for an additional two years. Applicants must earn at least $3,000 per month from foreign sources and hold valid health insurance. Costa Rica does not tax foreign-sourced income for visa holders.


For many remote workers today, Costa Rica is no longer just a travel destination, it is becoming a real base for building a sustainable life abroad.


## **What is the Costa Rica digital nomad visa?**


The Costa Rica Digital Nomad Visa is a residence programme designed for remote workers who want to live in the country while continuing to earn income from abroad. It is part of Costa Rica’s broader effort to attract location-independent professionals who contribute to the local economy without taking local jobs or relying on domestic employers. Unlike traditional short-stay tourism, this visa gives remote workers a legal pathway to stay longer and build a more stable base in the country.


Launched in 2021, the visa is specifically for non-Costa Rican remote workers who earn their income from outside the country. It is aimed at freelancers, employees of foreign companies, and entrepreneurs whose clients or businesses are based internationally. The duration is initially two years, with the option to renew for an additional two years, making it a flexible medium-term relocation option for digital nomads.


One of the biggest advantages is that Costa Rica does not tax foreign-sourced income under this visa, making it financially attractive for remote earners. It is also important to distinguish it from programmes like the pensionado or rentista visas, which are designed for retirees or individuals with passive income rather than active remote professionals.

## **Costa Rica digital nomad visa eligibility**


To qualify for the Costa Rica digital nomad visa, you must meet specific financial, professional, and legal requirements designed to ensure you can support yourself while working remotely from the country.


- **Minimum monthly income:** You must earn at least $3,000 per month from verified foreign sources. If applying with dependents, the required income threshold is higher. This ensures you can sustain living costs in Costa Rica without local employment.
- **Foreign income requirement:** Your income must come entirely from outside Costa Rica, whether from a remote job, freelance clients, or an international business. You are not permitted to work for Costa Rican employers under this visa.
- **Health insurance coverage:** You must hold valid international health insurance that covers medical treatment in Costa Rica for the full duration of your stay.
- **Clean criminal record:** Applicants must submit a police clearance certificate from their country of residence or citizenship showing no serious criminal history.
- **Proof of remote work:** You must provide evidence of employment or freelance contracts confirming that your work can be performed remotely, such as an employment letter, client agreements, or business registration.


## **Required documents for the Costa Rica digital nomad visa**


- **Valid passport and application form:** You need a passport with sufficient validity for your intended stay, along with a completed Costa Rica digital nomad visa application form submitted to the immigration authorities.
- **Proof of income:** You must show evidence of earning at least $3,000 per month from foreign sources. This can include three months of bank statements, payslips, or verified client contracts that clearly demonstrate consistent remote income.
- **Remote work documentation:** An employment letter confirming your remote work arrangement or freelance contracts is required. This proves that your income is earned outside Costa Rica and that your work can be performed digitally.
- **Health insurance:** You must provide a valid health insurance certificate that covers medical treatment in Costa Rica for the entire duration of your stay under the digital nomad visa.
- **Criminal background check:** A police clearance certificate from your home country or country of residence is required, often apostilled to confirm authenticity and ensure you meet security requirements.
- **Proof of address and supporting documents:** You may need to show proof of accommodation in Costa Rica, such as a rental agreement or booking, along with any additional documents requested by immigration to support your application.


## **How to apply for the Costa Rica Digital nomad visa**


Applications for the Costa Rica digital nomad visa can be submitted either through the Costa Rican immigration authority (DGME) while in Costa Rica or through a Costa Rican consulate abroad. Before starting, make sure you meet the income, insurance, and remote work requirements, as incomplete applications can slow down processing.


**Step 1:** Gather all required documents, including your passport, proof of income, employment or freelance documentation, health insurance certificate, and completed application form.


**Step 2:** Obtain a criminal background check from your home country or country of residence and have it apostilled. This is an important requirement and should be completed before submission.


**Step 3:** Submit your application either at a DGME office in Costa Rica or through an authorised Costa Rican consulate in your country.


**Step 4:** Pay the applicable application fee and retain proof of payment for your records.


**Step 5:** Wait for the authorities to review your documents and verify your eligibility. Processing times can vary depending on application volume and the completeness of your submission. Once approved, you can legally relocate to Costa Rica and begin your stay as a digital nomad.


## Costa Rica digital nomad visa: cost, duration, renewal and tax explained


The Costa Rica digital nomad visa is relatively affordable compared to many similar programmes. Applicants pay a $100 USD processing fee when submitting their application, plus an additional $90 USD for legal stay documentation and contributions to the country's Special Social Immigration Fund. To qualify, you must also demonstrate a stable monthly income of at least[$3,000 USD](http://migracion.go.cr/) from sources outside Costa Rica.


The visa is initially granted for one year, allowing remote workers to legally live and work in Costa Rica while earning income from foreign employers or clients. Although the first approval covers a single year, the programme allows a total stay of up to two years, making it suitable for nomads looking for a medium-term base rather than a short-term relocation.


Renewal is available once for an additional one-year period. To remain eligible, you must submit your renewal application at least 30 days before your initial visa expires and continue to meet the programme requirements. One of the biggest advantages is Costa Rica's territorial tax system. This means income earned outside Costa Rica is generally not subject to Costa Rican income tax, making the visa particularly attractive for foreign remote workers.


## **Frequently asked questions**


#### **Can you apply for the Costa Rica digital nomad visa while already in Costa Rica?**


Yes. One advantage of the programme is that applications can be submitted through Costa Rica's immigration authority while you are already in the country. Many remote workers enter as tourists first, explore potential locations, and then apply if they decide Costa Rica is a suitable long-term base. Ensure your tourist status remains valid throughout the process.


#### **Can family members join you on the Costa Rica digital nomad visa?**


Yes. The programme allows dependants such as spouses and children to accompany the main applicant. However, higher income requirements may apply when including family members. You will also need to provide supporting documentation proving the relationship and ensure health insurance coverage extends to accompanying dependents during their stay.


#### **Will Costa Rica tax your foreign-earned income?**


One of the biggest attractions of the visa is Costa Rica's territorial tax system. Income earned from clients, employers, or businesses located outside Costa Rica is generally not subject to Costa Rican income tax. However,[tax obligations](https://grey.co/blog/digital-nomad-tax) may still exist in your home country, so professional tax advice is recommended before relocating.


#### **How much does it cost to live in Costa Rica as a digital nomad?**


Costs vary depending on location and lifestyle. Beach towns[popular with expats](https://grey.co/blog/expat-guide-costa-rica) tend to be more expensive than inland cities. Many digital nomads spend between $1,500 and $3,500 per month covering accommodation, food, transport, internet, and leisure activities. Careful budgeting can significantly reduce costs, especially outside tourist hotspots.


#### **Can the Costa Rica digital nomad visa lead to permanent residency?**


The digital nomad visa is designed as a temporary residence pathway rather than a direct route to permanent residency. Holding the visa does not automatically qualify you for permanent residence. If long-term settlement is your goal, you may need to explore other immigration categories available under Costa Rican immigration law.


#### **How long does the Costa Rica digital nomad visa process take?**


Processing times vary depending on application volume and document verification. Many applicants receive a decision within several weeks, although timelines can extend if additional information is requested. Having complete documentation, including apostilled records and proof of income, can help avoid delays and improve the overall application experience.
